Although all AEs are recorded in the CRF after signing informed consent, SAE reporting to the sponsor begins after the patient has signed informed consent and has received investigational product. However, if an SAE occurs after signing informed consent, but prior to receiving investigational product, AND is considered reasonably possibly related to a study procedure then it MUST be reported.

Pregnancy (maternal or paternal exposure to investigational product) does not meet the definition of an AE. However, to fulfill regulatory requirements any pregnancy should be reported following the SAE process to collect data on the outcome for both mother and fetus.

Nonserious AEs obtained through the questionnaire are recorded and analyzed separately. Only SAEs elicited through the Nasal and Non-nasal Score Questionnaire and Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale are to be recorded as AEs via CRF and reported to Lilly or its designee within 24 hours as SAEs.

data.text: For the purposes of this study, an overdose of LY900018 or IMG is considered any dose that is higher than the assigned dose. Refer to the LY900018 IB and GlucaGen Summary of Product Characteristics for more information.

Blood pressure and pulse rate should be measured after at least 5 minutes supine. Unscheduled orthostatic vital signs should be assessed, if possible, during any AE of dizziness or posture-induced symptoms. If orthostatic measurements are required, patients should be supine for at least 5 minutes and stand for at least 2 minutes. If the patient feels unable to stand, supine vital signs only will be recorded.
Single ECGs will be collected and stored locally at the investigator's site. Triplicate ECGs will be electronically transmitted to a central ECG laboratory designated by Lilly.

If a hypoglycemic event meets the criteria of severe, it needs to be recorded as serious in the CRF (that is, recorded as an SAE). In the case of a hypoglycemic event (other than severe), the actual glucose value, if measured, should be recorded in the CRF, with any treatments administered, and not be recorded as an AE.
Cases of hypoglycemia may be treated with foods rich in carbohydrate such as fruit, juice, skimmed milk, or energy bars.

The bedside PG level, measured using a glucose analyzer (Antsense Duo, HORIBA Ltd. or equivalent), must be 90 to 250 mg/dL to start the procedure. If the bedside PG is outside of this range, the hypoglycemia induction should be rescheduled.

If the target bedside PG level cannot be achieved within 4 hours after the start of insulin infusion, the hypoglycemia induction procedure will be terminated before glucagon administration, and the patient may have a carbohydrate-rich meal and be discharged from the CRU after medical assessment. The patient may be rescheduled for a new dosing visit 1 to 7 days later.

data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
data.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
data.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) or type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia, meeting all eligibility criteria (Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Population - all randomized patients completing both periods with evaluable primary outcome (at least 66 patients, including at least 30 T1DM and 30 T2DM)) Summary measure: Difference in proportions (percentage of patients achieving treatment success: IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

data.name: Male contraception agreement
data.text: male patients: agree to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study and for 28 days following the last study treatment

data.name: Female contraception and pregnancy requirements
data.text: female patients: [3a] women of childbearing potential who are abstinent (if this is complete abstinence, as their preferred and usual lifestyle) or in a same sex relationship (as part of their preferred and usual lifestyle) must agree to either remain abstinent or stay in a same sex relationship without sexual relationships with males. Periodic abstinence (eg, calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, post-ovulation methods), declaration of abstinence just for the duration of a trial, and withdrawal are not acceptable methods of contraception. [3b] otherwise, women of childbearing potential participating must agree to use one highly effective method (less than 1% failure rate) of contraception, or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception for the entirety of the study. [A] women of childbearing potential participating must test negative for pregnancy prior to initiation of treatment as indicated by a negative serum pregnancy test at the screening visit followed by a negative urine pregnancy test within 24 hours prior to exposure. [B] either one highly effective method of contraception or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception will be used. The patient may choose to use a double barrier method of contraception. Barrier protection methods without concomitant use of a spermicide are not a reliable or acceptable method. Thus, each barrier method must include use of a spermicide. It should be noted that the use of male and female condoms as a double barrier method is not considered acceptable due to the high failure rate when these methods are combined. [3c] women not of childbearing potential may participate, and include those who are: [A] infertile due to surgical sterilization (hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, or tubal ligation), congenital anomaly such as mullerian agenesis; Or [B] postmenopausal, defined as either: [i] a woman at least 50 years of age with an intact uterus, not on hormone therapy, who has had either: [a] cessation of menses for at least 1 year, or [b] at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea with a follicle-stimulating hormone >40 mIU/mL; or [ii] a woman 55 or older not on hormone therapy, who has had at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea, or [iii] a woman at least 55 years of age with a diagnosis of menopause prior to starting hormone replacement therapy

data.text: After single-dose administration and up to 4 hours of PK/PD sampling and at least 6 hours in the CRU, patients are discharged and enter a washout period of 3 to 14 days.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow-up Transition

data.text: Patients with treatment-emergent antidrug antibodies at the follow-up/ED visit transition to additional immunogenicity follow-up every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Safety Gate Before Dosing Remaining Patients
data.text: The remaining patients will be dosed only after review and confirmation of safety data from the first 6 patients who complete Period 2 Day 1 (no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure).

data.name: Rescheduling of Admission for Out-of-Range Plasma Glucose
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1, delaying hypoglycemia induction and study treatment administration.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop Rule
data.text: Insulin infusion to induce hypoglycemia is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL; approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered.

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Glucagon Response
data.text: Procedures for insufficient response to glucagon administration will be followed (Section 9.2.4); a carbohydrate-rich meal and, if needed, a prandial insulin dose are administered after completion of PK sampling with investigator confirmation of stable PG.

data.name: Discontinuation for Enrollment in Other Research
data.text: Patients will be discontinued for enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation for Medical/Safety/Regulatory Reasons
data.text: Patients will be discontinued if participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation by Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken and Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation by Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Discontinuation of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: If a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria was inadvertently enrolled, the patient is discontinued unless the Lilly CP/CRP and investigator agree and documented approval is obtained to continue with or without continued treatment with investigational product.

data.name: Study-Level Termination for Safety
data.text: Following the review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED) Visit
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow-up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities, including the Follow-up/ED visit (within 28±2 days after last study treatment).

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome plus the follow-up visit 26 to 30 days (28±2 days) after the last study treatment; patients with TE ADA complete additional immunogenicity follow-up until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow-up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site after diligent attempts.

data.name: Discontinuation of the Study (Sponsor/Investigator)
data.description: The study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the investigator and sponsor following the safety review of the first 6 patients completing Period 2 Day 1.

data.name: Exit Due to Ineligibility (Inadvertent Enrollment)
data.description: Patients identified as not meeting enrollment criteria who were inadvertently enrolled are discontinued unless documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP permits continuation; such patients may be replaced up to a maximum of 75 enrolled.

data.name: Admission Eligibility Decision (Plasma Glucose)
data.description: At each period Day 1, determine whether PG is 90 to 250 mg/dL and insulin regimen is acceptable; otherwise reschedule admission.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop / Dosing Decision
data.description: During hypoglycemia induction, bedside PG monitoring determines when PG <60 mg/dL, triggering infusion stop and study treatment administration approximately 5 minutes later (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision After First 6 Patients
data.description: After the first 6 patients complete Period 2 Day 1, the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist decide whether to dose the remaining patients or stop the study for patient safety.

data.name: Glucagon Response Assessment Decision
data.description: Post glucagon administration, assess response; if insufficient response, follow rescue procedures (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Discharge Decision
data.description: At 6 hours after glucagon administration, decide whether the patient may be discharged following a carbohydrate-rich meal and stable PG, or remain inpatient at the investigator's discretion.

data.name: Immunogenicity Follow-up Decision
data.description: At the follow-up/ED visit, determine TE ADA status; if positive, schedule additional samples every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Primary Non-inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: Primary analysis comparing treatment success percentages; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 2-sided 95% CI for (IMG - LY900018) is less than 10%.

data.name: Patient Replacement Decision
data.description: If a patient discontinues before completing both periods with evaluable primary outcome, decide on replacement (not beyond 75 patients enrolled).
